description: This team is constituted to explore the undiscovered details about space. We wonder what else we are able to find.
summary: We developed an 8-chapter digital children's storybook featuring rich illustrations and narrative storytelling that humanizes historical space hardware left behind on the Moon and Mars. The project follows iconic artifacts such as Surveyor 1, Opportunity, and Apollo descent stages and bridges them to modern active missions like Perseverance. The project directly addresses the competition theme "Abandoned but not Forgotten" by transforming discarded technological relics into space guardians that rest peacefully under Martian sand and lunar dust. Using authentic historical data sourced from the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDC), the narrative grounds fictionalized emotional resonance in accurate scientific parameters regarding spacecraft locations and operational statuses. This project inspires primary school children (ages 6–10) by fostering STEM curiosity, teaching space history and reframing retired machinery not as "space junk" but as a proud legacy of exploration that paves the way for tomorrow’s generation of space travelers.
details:
Abandoned Guardians of the Space Cities is an interactive, 8-chapter digital children’s storybook designed for young readers aged 6 to 10. Built around authentic mission records from the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA), the book introduces children to retired and dormant NASA spacecraft including Surveyor 1, Apollo lunar descent stages, and the Opportunity rover—while connecting their historical achievements to active modern explorers like Perseverance. Through double-page illustrated spreads, touch-inspired "spectral viewfinder" visual cues, and accessible narrative storytelling, young readers discover where these machines rest today, what scientific discoveries they made, and how they communicate across space.

Children often view retired space hardware as broken machinery or "space junk". Our project reframes these artifacts as silent, heroic guardians that paved the way for human and robotic exploration. By translating technical archival data into emotionally resonant storytelling, the book sparks early curiosity in STEM, planetary science and aerospace engineering, makes real NASA mission history and archival records approachable for elementary-level learners and encourages the next generation of explorers to see space exploration as a continuous and collaborative journey across decades.

NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA) Master Catalog was used to verify spacecraft launch timelines, mission parameters, planetary locations and current operational statuses. Google Gemini was used to handle troubleshooting, fixing slight errors in the coding and debugging. A website was created to compile the 16-page double-spread book format.

Our team blended rigorous archival accuracy with a warm, tactile storybook aesthetic styled like an interactive digital tablet for Abandoned but not Forgotten challenge. Key factors we considered included age-appropriate pedagogy, visual and textual clarity, compliance and attribution management. We balanced real scientific concepts such as Martian dust storms cleaning solar panels and deep-space radio relays with imaginative metaphors tailored for ages 6–10. We also iteratively refined every spread to ensure clean typography, high contrast, and accurate depictions of historic landers and rovers. Finally, we made sure we ensured zero unauthorized modification of official NASA logos and documented the necessary NSSDCA data sources.
